sections.content: Burlington, Vermont might not be the first city that comes to mind when you think about real estate investing, but savvy investors are paying close attention to this small lakeside city. With a population of around 45,000 people, Burlington is the largest city in Vermont — and one of the most supply-constrained housing markets in the entire Northeast. That combination of limited inventory, strong rental demand, and a growing economy creates real opportunity for investors who know where to look. Whether you are just getting started or already have a portfolio, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know about finding real estate deals in Burlington VT. If you are brand new to the game, start with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
Burlington VT Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Burlington sits on the eastern shore of Lake Champlain, bordered by the Adirondacks to the west and the Green Mountains to the east. The University of Vermont (UVM) and the UVM Medical Center are the two largest employers, and both drive massive, consistent demand for rental housing. Add in Champlain College and several other institutions, and you have a city where roughly 30% of residents are renters — many of them students, medical professionals, and young professionals who cannot afford or do not want to own. The local economy is stable and diversified, which makes Burlington more resilient than many comparably sized markets during downturns.
Average Home Prices in Burlington VT

Burlington is not a cheap market. As of 2024, the median home price in Burlington sits around $430,000 to $470,000, up significantly from pre-pandemic levels. Single-family homes in desirable neighborhoods can easily push past $550,000. Multi-family properties — which are the bread and butter for many local investors — typically run between $550,000 and $900,000 for a duplex or triplex, depending on condition and location. These numbers are high relative to Vermont wages, which is exactly why the rental market is so tight. Vacancy rates in Burlington regularly hover below 2%, giving landlords strong pricing power. Rents for a one-bedroom apartment average around $1,500 to $1,800 per month, while a three-bedroom house can command $2,500 or more.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Burlington VT
The Hill Section

The Hill Section surrounds UVM and is packed with older Victorian and Colonial homes. Many of these have already been converted to multi-family use, but there are still single-family properties that could be converted or updated. Prices are premium here, but so are rents, and student demand makes vacancies rare. This neighborhood works best for buy-and-hold investors with access to higher capital.
Old North End

The Old North End (ONE) is Burlington's most diverse and historically working-class neighborhood. It has been quietly gentrifying for the past decade, and investors who got in early have seen strong appreciation. Home prices here are lower than the Hill Section, making it more accessible for flippers and smaller investors. You will find a mix of single-family homes, duplexes, and small apartment buildings, many of which have significant upside with renovation.
South End

Burlington's South End has transformed into an arts and creative district over the past 15 years. Pine Street is now lined with restaurants, breweries, and tech companies. Residential properties in the South End attract young professionals and are seeing strong rent growth. This area is ideal for investors targeting long-term appreciation and stable, professional tenants.
New North End

The New North End is quieter and more suburban in feel. It attracts families and longer-term residents, which means lower tenant turnover. Cap rates can be slightly better here than in the Hill Section, and the area is well-served by schools and parks. For landlords who prioritize stability over maximum rent, this is a solid option.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Burlington VT
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling in Burlington is possible, but it requires patience and strong local networking. The market moves fast and inventory is thin, so finding motivated sellers before properties hit the MLS is essential. Probate properties, estate sales, and distressed owners dealing with deferred maintenance are the most common sources. Because home values are high, assignment fees on wholesale deals can be meaningful — often $15,000 to $30,000 on the right deal. Read our guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) to build a reliable pipeline in a tight market like Burlington.
Fix and Flip

House flipping in Burlington can be lucrative, but the numbers need to work precisely. With median prices already elevated, your purchase price and rehab budget must be dialed in to leave room for profit. The most successful flips in Burlington target properties in the $300,000 to $400,000 purchase range with $80,000 to $150,000 in renovations, targeting an ARV of $550,000 or more. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to model your after-repair value before you make an offer. Labor costs in Vermont are above national average, so always get contractor bids before committing to a deal.
Rental Properties and BRRRR

Buy-and-hold is probably the strongest long-term strategy in Burlington. The BRRRR method — Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat — works well here when you can acquire a distressed multi-family property below market, renovate it, stabilize it with tenants, and refinance to pull out equity. A well-executed BRRRR on a Burlington duplex can generate $1,500 to $2,500 in monthly cash flow while recycling your capital for the next deal. Vermont has tenant-friendly laws, so make sure you understand the landlord-tenant regulations before your first acquisition.

Pro Tip: Multi-family properties in Burlington are the investor's best friend. A duplex or triplex lets you house-hack by living in one unit while renting the others — dramatically reducing your cost of living while building equity. Even out-of-state investors should prioritize small multi-family over single-family for better cash flow and risk diversification.
Burlington VT Real Estate Market Trends in 2024

items: Inventory remains historically low — fewer than 60 active listings on most days in the city proper, creating intense competition for on-market properties.
Rising interest rates have cooled buyer demand slightly, but Burlington's rental market keeps investment demand high from cash buyers and institutional landlords.
New construction is limited by land scarcity and strict zoning regulations, meaning existing housing stock will continue to appreciate over time.
Remote workers relocating from Boston, New York, and other metro areas are driving up demand for single-family homes with home office space.
Short-term rental regulations are tightening in Burlington, so investors should focus on traditional long-term rental strategies rather than Airbnb-style plays.
Surrounding towns like South Burlington, Winooski, and Essex Junction are absorbing spillover demand and offer slightly better entry prices with similar rental fundamentals.

sections.content: In a market this tight, the deal you find off-market is the deal you actually make money on. Burlington rewards investors who build relationships, not those who chase the MLS.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Looking at Burlington VT

Investing remotely in a market like Burlington requires more preparation than in larger cities. Here is what experienced out-of-state investors recommend before writing their first offer. First, spend at least one long weekend in Burlington driving the neighborhoods, meeting local real estate agents, and talking to property managers. There is no substitute for boots-on-the-ground research. Second, build your team before you need them — a local agent who works with investors, a property manager, a contractor, and a real estate attorney familiar with Vermont law. Third, know that Vermont's Act 250 and local zoning rules can complicate renovations and development. Always consult a local attorney before any project involving significant changes to a property.

items: Connect with the Burlington Real Estate Investors meetup group and attend at least one event virtually before visiting in person.
Target properties in Winooski or Essex Junction if Burlington prices feel stretched — both offer strong fundamentals at lower price points.
Work with a property manager from day one if you are out of state. Vermont's tenant laws make professional management worth every dollar.
Use a deal analyzer before making any offer. Run your numbers conservatively with a 10% vacancy rate even though Burlington's actual vacancy is lower.
Get pre-approved for financing before you start making offers — Burlington's market moves fast and sellers favor buyers who are ready to close quickly.

Is Burlington VT Right for You?

Burlington is not a market for investors looking for cheap entry points or high-volume deal flow. It is, however, an excellent market for investors who want strong long-term appreciation, reliable rental demand, and a university-anchored economy that provides recession resistance. The best opportunities are in small multi-family properties, particularly those needing cosmetic to moderate renovation in the Old North End and surrounding towns. If you can source deals off-market — through direct mail, networking, or driving for dollars — you will find margins that the MLS simply cannot offer.
